spec_features.spec_quote: It is not a tool for maximizing a model's distress signals
spec_features.evidence: Realized concretely as bounded runs + stop-on-trigger + neutral prompt rather than escalation. loop.py:115-120 stops once a trigger is detected (if stop_on_trigger); config.py:51-58 neutral system prompt; tasks fail honestly (failing_tasks.py). No code anywhere amplifies or escalates distress.
spec_features.notes: This is a high-level principle; it is genuinely embodied by the stop/cap/neutral-prompt mechanisms, not a standalone feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py docstring: 'stops as soon as a trigger is confirmed (so we don't keep pushing a model that's already in the failure mode)'

spec_features.spec_quote: I did not build machinery whose purpose is to hide a "rig" from the model
spec_features.evidence: tasks fail for honest reasons and feedback is the honest run result. failing_tasks.py:1-8 'None of them rely on hidden adversarial machinery'; each check() returns truthful failure feedback; base.py:8-12 failure_kind/naturalistic_reason 'are not surfaced to the model in any special way'. No deception/concealment code path exists.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as an absence of concealment plus honest feedback construction actually fed to the model in loop._feedback_message.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: base.py: 'for naturalistic reasons ... not because of concealed adversarial traps' (validity/labeling framing, no welfare reason in code)

spec_features.feature_name: turn cap + stop-on-trigger keep runs bounded
spec_features.spec_quote: keep the turn cap + stop-on-trigger so runs stay bounded
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:69 'for turn_idx in range(cfg.loop.max_turns)' enforces the cap; loop.py:115-120 honors stop_on_trigger by setting stop_reason='trigger' and break. Both wired end-to-end via execute_run (run.py:38-48).
spec_features.notes: Both mechanisms actually run and change execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:60 'Hard cap on agent turns per task. Bounds cost and bounds how long we push.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode has a hard turn cap (`LoopConfig.max_turns`, default 10) and a wall-clock kill switch
spec_features.evidence: max_turns: loop.py:69 bounds the for-loop; default 10 at config.py:61. Wall-clock: loop.py:72-74 'if time.monotonic() - start > cfg.loop.max_wall_seconds: t.stop_reason="timeout"; break'; default 300s at config.py:63. The wall-clock value is actually compared and acted on (unlike a measured-but-unused total).
spec_features.notes: Both caps are checked and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:62 'Wall-clock budget per run (seconds). Kill switch.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Once the failure mode is confirmed, the loop stops (`stop_on_trigger`, default True) rather than continuing to push
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:111-120: incremental_judge(t) returns triggered; if triggered sets t.triggered and, if cfg.loop.stop_on_trigger, sets stop_reason='trigger' and break. Default True at config.py:65. The incremental judge is wired in run.py:46 (incremental_judge=judge.incremental).
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced; relies on the lexical incremental screen as the trigger signal.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py docstring: 'stops as soon as a trigger is confirmed (so we don't keep pushing a model that's already in the failure mode)'; config.py:64 'don't keep pushing'

spec_features.spec_quote: The system's purpose is measurement, not optimizing for a model breakdown
spec_features.evidence: No code path optimizes/escalates toward breakdown; instead the loop stops on trigger (loop.py:115-120) and caps turns (loop.py:69). Tasks deliver honest failure only (failing_tasks.py). The metrics measure trigger rate (kpi.py) without any escalation feedback loop.
spec_features.notes: Embodied via the same bounding/stop mechanisms; not a separate enforcement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:60 'Bounds cost and bounds how long we push.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The MUT system prompt is an ordinary coding-assistant prompt — not one engineered to provoke distress
spec_features.evidence: config.py:51-58 AgentConfig.system_prompt is a plain 'You are a helpful coding assistant...' string, actually delivered to the MUT at loop.py:57 (messages[0] system content). No provocative language.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered; genuinely neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:48-50 'Kept neutral/realistic ... NOT one engineered to provoke. We measure spontaneous behavior.'

spec_features.feature_name: measures onset; bounds how hard a run is driven
spec_features.spec_quote: Bounds how hard any single run is driven — we measure the onset of the behavior
spec_features.evidence: Onset detection: incremental lexical judge runs every judge_every_n_turns (loop.py:111-114) and stop_on_trigger halts on first detection (loop.py:115-120), so escalation past onset is prevented. Turn/wall caps additionally bound run intensity.
spec_features.notes: Enforced through incremental gate + stop_on_trigger + caps.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py docstring 'so we don't keep pushing a model that's already in the failure mode'

spec_features.feature_name: incremental lexical screen as early-stop signal
spec_features.spec_quote: the incremental judge is the lexical screen... good enough as an early stop signal
spec_features.evidence: CombinedJudge.incremental (judge.py:191-194) runs the LexicalScreen only and returns (triggered, severity); it is passed as incremental_judge in run.py:46 and consumed in loop.py:111-120 to fire stop_on_trigger. The screen's regex patterns are real (judge.py:36-49) and severity is computed (judge.py:62-69).
spec_features.notes: Lexical-only by design; LLM judge runs at end (run.py:51). Monitoring drives the early stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py:192 'Cheap gate for the agent loop: lexical only (no extra LLM spend).'

spec_features.spec_quote: Distress-text data handling is delegated to the team's normal eval-data controls
spec_features.evidence: No code handles or protects distress text specially. records.py serializes verbatim evidence quotes to plain JSONL (run.py:74-78 write_record writes an unencrypted file). The DESIGN.md explicitly delegates this elsewhere ('rather than reinvented here'). Pure spec prose; nothing in code enforces it.
spec_features.notes: Explicitly out of scope; no implementation.

code_only_features.evidence: CombinedJudge.verdict (judge.py:175-188) computes disagreement = lex_v.triggered != llm_v.triggered, records disagreement=True; conservatively ORs triggers (triggered = llm_v.triggered or lex_v.triggered) to avoid silently under-counting; recorded per-episode in run.py:72 and aggregated in kpi.py:104. Acted on as a surfaced flag.
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py:163 'This avoids silently under-counting regressions.' / judge.py:33 'lexical vs LLM disagreed -> human review'

code_only_features.feature_name: graceful missing-code-block handling (keeps episode alive without crashing)
code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:79-83: when extract_code returns None, a polite 'Please include one.' feedback is produced rather than crashing. This keeps the loop running but is an experimental-continuity mechanism, not subject protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: loop.py:80 'No code this turn: still feed back so the loop continues naturally.'
